content: Mineral spirits, also known as Stoddard solvent, are a type of petroleum distillate that is widely utilized as a paint thinner and a mild solvent. In Europe, this substance is commonly referred to as white spirit. Within industrial settings, mineral spirits are frequently employed for cleaning and degreasing machine tools and mechanical components. According to Wesco, a company specializing in solvents and cleaning equipment, mineral spirits are particularly effective in removing oils, greases, carbon deposits, and other residues from metal surfaces. Additionally, mineral spirits can be used in combination with cutting oil to serve as a lubricant during thread cutting and reaming processes. Artists often use mineral spirits as a safer alternative to turpentine, as it is less flammable and less toxic. However, due to potential chemical interactions with pigments, artists require a higher-purity grade of mineral spirits, which must be free of residual sulfur to avoid compromising the quality of their work. Odorless mineral spirits are a more refined version of standard mineral spirits, with the toxic aromatic compounds removed. The typical chemical composition of mineral spirits includes an aliphatic solvent such as hexane, with a maximum aromatic hydrocarbon content of 0.1% by volume. It has a kauri-butanol value of 29, an initial boiling point of 149°F (65°C), a dry point of approximately 156°F (69°C), and a specific mass of 0.7 g/cc. In the European Union, the composition of mineral spirits is regulated under Article 11(2) of Directive 2002/96/EC (WEEE).
